dhpak2.4:1.1: 2.4 The Story about the Fool’s Festival
dhpak2.4:2.1: “They cultivate heedlessness,” {1.256} this Dhamma teaching was given by the
dhpak2.4:2.2: Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to the Fools’ Festival.
dhpak2.4:3.1: For on a certain date there was a festival proclaimed in Sāvatthī called Fools’ Festival, and
dhpak2.4:3.2: on the occasion of this festival foolish, unintelligent folk used to smear their bodies with
dhpak2.4:3.3: ashes and cow-dung and for a period of seven days go about uttering all manner of coarse talk.
dhpak2.4:3.4: At this time they felt no shame when they met kinsfolk or friends
dhpak2.4:3.5: or renunciants, but stood in the doorways and uttered coarse talk.
dhpak2.4:3.6: Those who could not endure the coarse talk
dhpak2.4:3.7: would pay the holiday-makers half a kahāpaṇa, a quarter, or a whole kahāpaṇa, according to their means,
dhpak2.4:3.8: and the holiday-makers would take the money and depart from their houses.
dhpak2.4:4.1: Now at this time there were in Sāvatthī fifty million of noble disciples, and they sent word
dhpak2.4:4.2: to the Teacher: “Venerable Sir, let the Fortunate One refrain for a period of seven days
dhpak2.4:4.3: from entering the city with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus; let him instead remain at the monastery.”
dhpak2.4:4.4: And for a period of seven days the noble disciples caused food to be prepared for the Saṅgha
dhpak2.4:4.5: of bhikkhus at the monastery and sent it to them, but did not themselves leave their houses.
dhpak2.4:5.1: On the eighth day, however, when the festival was at an end, they invited the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha to be their guests,
dhpak2.4:5.2: escorted them into the city, and gave abundant offerings. And having seated themselves [28.311] respectfully on one side,
dhpak2.4:5.3: they said to the Teacher: “Venerable Sir, we have spent the past seven days in great distress. Our ears had
dhpak2.4:5.4: like to burst from hearing the coarse talk of foolish folk. {1.257} No one felt any shame before anybody
dhpak2.4:5.5: else, and for this reason we did not permit you to enter the city. We ourselves did not go out of the house.”
dhpak2.4:6.1: The Teacher listened to what they said, and then replied: “After this manner do foolish, stupid men
dhpak2.4:6.2: conduct themselves. But they that are intelligent preserve heedfulness as their greatest treasure, and
dhpak2.4:6.3: by so doing at last attain the Deathless, Great Nibbāna.” So saying, he pronounced the following verses:
dhpak2.4:7.1: Foolish, stupid people cultivate heedlessness, the sage guards heedfulness just as his greatest wealth.
dhpak2.4:8.1: Do not cultivate heedlessness, do not cultivate attachment to sensual
dhpak2.4:8.2: pleasures, the heedful one, meditating, surely attains great happiness.
dhpak2.4:10.1: At the conclusion of the verse many became Stream-enterers and so on, and the Dhamma teaching was beneficial to many people.
